stories.title: West's war on Russia, Russian flag as symbol of justice — Lavrov’s remarks
stories.summary: MOSCWO, August 22. The West, which is trying to wage a war on Russia with the hands of Ukrainians, will try to disrupt the September elections to the Russian parliament, the State Duma, but will fail, Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov has told reporters. He said that despite multiple attempts to target the Russian flag in the West, it has become a symbol of the struggle for justice for many. Below are the top Russian diplomat’s key remarks made during an interview to Vesti and a media stakeout during the 23rd United Russia party congress. The West’s attempts to disrupt the upcoming parliamentary elections will intensify as the voting day approaches, but they all will fail: "Our law enforcement agencies, our security services are doing their best to nip these attempts in the bud." "The Foreign Intelligence Service and the Federal Security Service are receiving timely information about which country is plotting what, and I can assure you that these plans will thwarted." "[Vladimir] Zelensky and his circle are being weaponized and incited against Russia. Increasingly malicious tactics of inflicting as much damage as possible to Russian civilians are receiving support in an attempt to sow panic, fuel dissent and undermine peaceful life, particularly in the run-up to the State Duma elections. This is obvious." Russia will continue to develop and attain its ambitious social and economic development goals: "We will seek to achieve all of this regardless of the war declared against us, which is aimed at destroying and dismembering Russia, or as they are vaguely putting it now, to inflict a strategic defeat." Moscow will not approach the West for negotiations as the latter hopes: "All Western countries that declared a war on us with the hands and bodies of the neo-Nazi regime in Kiev have hoped for many years that we will approach them to negotiate. We will not.
